t: Spain’s viceroyalty for South America, ruled from Lima, which at first covered nearly all of Spanish South America.
Silver from Potosí, mined with forced mita labour, financed the Spanish crown and flowed to Europe and China.
Bourbon reforms cut its territory in the eighteenth century, and the Battle of Ayacucho in 1824 ended Spanish rule.
dyk: The first book printed in South America was a catechism in Spanish, Quechua and Aymara, published in Lima in 1584.
ev: The New Laws of Charles V create the Viceroyalty of Peru
Silver is discovered at the Cerro Rico of Potosí
The University of San Marcos is founded in Lima
Túpac Amaru, last ruler of the Neo-Inca State, is executed in Cuzco
An earthquake and tsunami destroy much of Lima and the port of Callao
Upper Peru and Potosí pass to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
The rebellion of Túpac Amaru II begins in the southern Andes
Sucre defeats the royalists at the Battle of Ayacucho

f.founder: Charles V (by the New Laws of 1542)
f.predecessor: Governorates of New Castile and New Toledo; Inca Empire
f.successor: Republic of Peru; Viceroyalties of New Granada and the Río de la Plata
